title: The Present Indicative Active of ω-Verbs
subtitle: λύω, λύεις, λύει — the foundation of the verb system.
objectives: Conjugate any regular ω-verb in the present indicative active.
Understand the thematic vowel ο/ε and its role in conjugation.
Translate present indicative active verbs in context.

sections.heading: The thematic verb
sections.body:
Most Greek verbs are thematic verbs. They are called thematic because they insert a thematic vowel (ο or ε) between the stem and the personal ending. The thematic vowel is ο before μ and ν; it is ε everywhere else.

The present tense expresses action happening now or action happening habitually. λύω means 'I am loosing' or 'I loose'. Greek does not distinguish 'I loose' from 'I am loosing' the way English does. Context tells you whether the action is momentary or ongoing.

sections.heading: The present indicative active: λύω (I loose, I free)
sections.body:
singular
  1st   λύω         I loose
  2nd   λύεις       you loose
  3rd   λύει        he/she/it looses

  plural
  1st   λύομεν      we loose
  2nd   λύετε       you (plural) loose
  3rd   λύουσι(ν)   they loose

The stem is λυ-. The thematic vowel is ο/ε. The personal endings are -ω, -εις, -ει, -ομεν, -ετε, -ουσι(ν).

The third person plural adds a movable ν: λύουσιν when the next word begins with a vowel or at the end of a sentence.

sections.heading: Other examples
sections.body:
παύω (I stop): παύω, παύεις, παύει, παύομεν, παύετε, παύουσι(ν)

γράφω (I write): γράφω, γράφεις, γράφει, γράφομεν, γράφετε, γράφουσι(ν)

λέγω (I say, I speak): λέγω, λέγεις, λέγει, λέγομεν, λέγετε, λέγουσι(ν)

The pattern is universal. Once you know it, you can conjugate any regular ω-verb in the present indicative active.

sections.heading: A sentence from Xenophon
sections.body:
Anabasis I.1.2: οἱ δὲ παῖδες παιδεύονται.
'And the boys are educated.' παιδεύονται is third person plural middle/passive (you will learn the middle in Stage 3). The active form would be παιδεύουσι — 'they educate.'

sections.heading: Self-check
sections.instructions: Cover the answers. Conjugate or answer.

items.answer: ο before μ and ν; ε everywhere else.

sections.heading: Up next
sections.body: Lesson 2.12 introduces adjectives of the first and second declension: ἀγαθός, ἀγαθή, ἀγαθόν. Adjectives agree with nouns in gender, number, and case. They can be used attributively (the good man) or predicatively (the man is good). The distinction is marked by position.

lesson_completion.criteria: Mark the lesson complete when you can conjugate any regular ω-verb in the present indicative active from memory in under sixty seconds and can translate ten present-tense sentences without error.
